column1: The exposition here builds on the expectations theory of the term structure. For a systematic discussion of the theory of the term structure, see Cox, Ingersoll, and Ross (1985); Shiller (1990); or Campbell and Shiller (1991). Under the expectations hypothesis of the term structure, long-term nominal interest rates depend on expectations of future nominal short-term interest rates. These future short-term rates will be functions of monetary policy, so expectations about future policy play an important role in determining the shape of the term structure.
